clue.text: Revolutionary on white horse hesitated

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the revolutionary after the white horse

parts.note: a white horse is a breaking wave with a foaming crest
a revolutionary is a Red, a communist

explanation.surface: A rebel on a pale steed held back at the decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The white horse is a crested wave at sea, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver is to be undecided and falter, a synonym for hesitating.

clue.text: Toy revolver can give one a fair turn

definitions.text: can give one a fair turn
definitions.meaning: a fairground merry-go-round gives riders a ride round

explanation.surface: A child's pretend gun can be a fun thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a spinning toy top and a fairground roundabout.

clue.text: Hamlet is offensive about young woman who's upset

indicators.note: about means the nasty word goes round the reversed girl

parts.note: vile means offensive or disgusting

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for the girl is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is rude to a distressed girl, like Ophelia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests the play, but it is a small settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small rural settlement, a little village.

clue.text: King without queen? What a beast!

parts.note: a king is royal
stag describes a party for men only, without women

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a monarch lacking his consort.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer with antlers of twelve or more points is a fine animal of that name.

clue.text: Failure rarely experienced by Grace Darling

definitions.meaning: a score of nought in cricket, which W.G. Grace, the great Victorian batsman, seldom made

explanation.surface: Grace Darling, the Victorian lighthouse heroine, seldom failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling was a famous lifeboat heroine, but the clue splits her name: W.G. Grace was a great English cricketer, and a zero score in cricket is a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer out without scoring has made a nought; it is also an affectionate pet name.

clue.text: Fellow beheaded king — what could be more appropriate?

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its first letter, so the fellow's opening letter goes

parts.note: a chappie is an informal word for a man or fellow
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A grim historical scene of a man decapitating a monarch, with a wry comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded king' suggests decapitating a monarch, but 'beheaded' acts on 'Fellow' and the king is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A happier choice of word is a more fitting, more felicitous one.

clue.text: Boss is on watch for poacher among staff

parts.note: the head is the boss or chief
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover

explanation.surface: The manager is keeping an eye out for someone stealing game on the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poacher' suggests game theft; here it is a recruiter luring staff from rival firms.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruiter who lures employees from other companies steals talent from rivals' workforces.

clue.text: Build house

explanation.surface: Construct a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means erect a building and also give a guest lodging.

clue.text: Partners occupying one elevated place in office

indicators.note: occupying means the partners sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
tall means high or elevated
N and S, north and south, are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: Colleagues hold a raised position at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts the bridge partners, North and South, inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to induct them formally into a post.

clue.text: Colour with which I had decorated again

parts.note: red is a colour
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone describes the colour they used when painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Redid is the past tense of redo, which can mean repaint or refurbish a room.

clue.text: One source of whisky I cut down

parts.note: to cut someone down is to kill or slay them

explanation.surface: A distiller boasts of felling something.
explanation.walkthrough: Islay is a Scottish island famous for its peaty malt whisky distilleries.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hebridean island is home to many malt distilleries, so it produces the spirit.

clue.text: It is quickly pursued outside and beaten

indicators.note: outside means the pursued word wraps around the short form of it is

parts.note: to chase is to pursue quickly
'tis is the poetic contraction of it is

explanation.surface: Something is hunted down in the open and given a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quickly pursued' is one piece, not an adverb on 'outside'; 'outside' puts it around the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastised can mean physically punished, thrashed or flogged.

clue.text: Responsible for island I left? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to put the three pieces down in the opposite order and backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are to blame for abandoning an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' reverses the whole run ISLAND-I-LEFT pieces, so the Napoleonic island comes out as a different word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being liable for something means being legally answerable or accountable for it.

clue.text: Paw on cat that's held by person in charge

definitions.text: that's held by person in charge

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the paw after the cat

parts.note: the cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip
a paw is an informal word for a hand

explanation.surface: A creature's foot resting on a cat, which someone has hold of.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is the flogging lash, the cat-o'-nine-tails, not a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the upper position of control is the idiom for whoever dominates a situation.

clue.text: Position, initially, of the joints is critical

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: articular means relating to the joints

explanation.surface: Where the joints sit is vital, says a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular person is fussy and exacting, quick to find fault.

clue.text: American's believed, we hear, to be a visitor

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: Americans say 'I guess' for 'I believe', so guessed means believed

explanation.surface: A US citizen is thought to be someone staying a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone invited to stay or dine, a caller or visitor.

clue.text: Fair play from uncle? Presumably

definitions.meaning: a game at a fairground where balls are thrown at a figure's head
an uncle is presumably on the side of his wife, the aunt

explanation.surface: Fairness from a relative, one supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional British fair and pub game of knocking a dummy off a post; the second reading splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground pastime is a figure pelted with sticks; a husband is presumably his wife's supporter.

clue.text: Goose is cooked, politician revealed

indicators.note: cooked suggests the two letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament
to let on is to reveal

explanation.surface: Someone's goose is cooked when a politician has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goose is cooked' looks like the idiom for being ruined; 'Goose' alone is the definition and 'is cooked' gives SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a silly, foolish person, a fool.

clue.text: Standard produced by police HQ staff

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters
a staff is a stick

explanation.surface: A benchmark set by headquarters personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring rod by which things are judged is a criterion or benchmark.

clue.text: Girl in thin silk

explanation.surface: A young woman in a flimsy garment.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a woman's name and a light, sheer crepe fabric named after a French dressmaker.

clue.text: Melodious arrangement for one harp

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders the letters given after it

explanation.surface: A tuneful score written for a single harp.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphean means tuneful like the music of Orpheus, the legendary Greek musician.

clue.text: Officer in difficult situation turned to other ranks

indicators.note: turned means the word for a tight spot is read backwards

parts.note: a jam is a predicament
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks

explanation.surface: An officer in trouble switches to the enlisted men.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is an army officer ranking above captain.

clue.text: A small vehicle's carrying Jack to a capital city

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
a kart is a small motor racing car

explanation.surface: A little car takes a man named Jack to a nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The small vehicle carries J at its front: J + A KART, then 'to a' adds the last A.
explanation.definitionFit: Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia.

clue.text: What produces a character with a kind appearance?

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a face is an outward appearance or look

explanation.surface: A question about what gives someone a benevolent look.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'character' here is a printed letter, not a person, and 'kind' is a noun, not 'friendly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A font design is what prints each letter or symbol.

clue.text: Leader of team demands lots of work

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to ask is to demand or request

explanation.surface: A team captain requires a heavy workload.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are jobs or assignments, so many of them make a heavy workload.

clue.text: His treasure was buried in a town in Wales

definitions.meaning: the pirate captain whose hoard is sought in Treasure Island
a town in north-east Wales, on the Dee estuary

explanation.surface: Someone hid his riches in a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Flint is the dead pirate of Stevenson's novel, and the name is also a Flintshire town.

clue.text: Quenches with a lot of water, in seconds

indicators.note: in means the body of water sits inside the two letters for seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so seconds gives two of them
a lake is a large body of water

explanation.surface: Someone puts out a fire with plenty of water in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake thirst is to satisfy or quench it.

clue.text: He can make what's originally yellow turn red on the outside

definitions.text: He can make what's originally yellow turn red on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the reversed colour wraps around the single letter
turn tells us to read the colour backwards
originally picks the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A craftsman can change a yellow cloth into a red one.
explanation.walkthrough: RED turned is DER, which goes round Y to give D-Y-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer is someone who colours fabric, so can change its hue.

clue.text: Detailed description one associate provided in unusual way

parts.note: a spec (specification) is a detailed description
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: A partner supplies a detailed account in an odd manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Specially means for a particular purpose, out of the ordinary rather than in the usual manner.

clue.text: The crew and I found lots of bones

parts.note: tars are sailors, so the crew of a ship

explanation.surface: Sailors and the speaker discover a heap of skeletal remains.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the small bones of the ankle, a group of seven in each foot.

clue.text: This politician's constituents aren't so stupid

definitions.note: possessive in the clue; the anagram's letters make up this politician

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A claim that the voters of a certain lawmaker are smarter than thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' says the letters of 'aren't so', jumbled ('stupid'), make up the word for the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of an upper legislative chamber such as the US Senate.

clue.text: Managed to fire rifle

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to sack someone is to fire them from a job

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in discharging a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' is a verb meaning search and plunder, not a gun; 'fire' means dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search through it thoroughly and plunder it.
